name: ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models are More Redundant Than You Expect
problem: Deep LMs contain many near-duplicate layers and some layers that barely affect function, but pruning them requires complex machinery.
mechanism: Defines BLOCK INFLUENCE (BI), a metric for a layer's significance in the LLM, computed from similarity between a layer's input and output hidden representations (cosine similarity: BI = 1 - max cos-sim means the layer changes the representation most). Pruning is then plain LAYER REMOVAL - delete the lowest-BI layers outright - rather than structured pruning with masks or low-rank approximations.
speedup_reported: Claims to significantly outperform prior state-of-the-art MODEL PRUNING methods, and is ORTHOGONAL to quantization-like methods, enabling further combined reduction in parameters and computation. NO numeric speedup multiplier is stated in the abstract, so speedup_reported deliberately records the qualitative claim and the orthogonality property rather than inventing a number. Pruning fraction and its effect on quality are in the paper body, not the abstract, and are not recorded here.
notes:
ADOPTION: research-only - layer removal is trivially implementable and hence widely TRIED, but no production engine ships a ShortGPT-derived depth configuration for any mainline checkpoint, because the layers to drop are checkpoint- and task-specific. INCLUDED because it is the cheapest possible depth-pruning result and therefore the control case against LayerSkip (pap-eff-layerskip) and Mixture-of-Depths (pap-eff-mixture-of-depths): it shows how much of the 'LLMs have redundant depth' claim is obtainable with NO training and NO early-exit machinery at all. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar and no venue in the arXiv comment, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Mar 2024). CAVEAT: pruning-by-removal is not lossless - quality degradation is traded against layer count - so it should never be cited as a lossless inference speedup, unlike every speculative-decoding record in this set.
